title: India's Asian Games 2026 Medal Tally: 85 Medals, Sport by Sport, With One Day to Go
excerpt: India has 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver, 37 bronze — after Day 14 in Aichi-Nagoya, with archery leading the gold count and athletics contributing the most medals overall.
body:
• India has won 85 medals — 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze — after Day 14 of the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026, with one day of competition remaining.
  • Archery is India's most successful sport with five golds, while athletics has contributed the most medals overall — 24 across gold, silver and bronze.
  • Both Indian cricket teams, both kabaddi teams and both hockey teams swept gold in every team-sport final they contested.
  • The Games close on October 4, with several finals — including boxing and wrestling title bouts — deciding the final tally.

With one day of competition remaining at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, India's athletes have delivered one of the country's strongest showings in the event's history — 85 medals through Day 14, spanning 21 sports and anchored by a sweep of the marquee team-sport golds.

The tally, sport by sport

The headline number breaks down as 21 gold, 27 silver and 37 bronze. Athletics leads the raw count with 24 medals (1 gold, 9 silver, 14 bronze), a reminder of India's deepening bench on the track and in the field. Shooting follows with 15 medals, including three golds — and the mixed trap pairing of Kynan Chenai and Neeru Dhanda set an Asian record of 34 in their final, according to organisers.

Archery has been the standout by gold count: five of India's 21 golds came from the range, with compound archers sweeping team titles and Kumkum Mohod adding the women's individual recurve crown. Boxing (three golds), wrestling (two) and the team sports round out the list.

The full sport-wise medal table, as of October 3:

  • Athletics: 1 gold, 9 silver, 14 bronze — 24 medals
  • Shooting: 3 gold, 8 silver, 4 bronze — 15 medals
  • Archery: 5 gold, 2 silver, 2 bronze — 9 medals
  • Boxing: 3 gold, 0 silver, 3 bronze — 6 medals
  • Wrestling: 2 gold, 2 silver, 2 bronze — 6 medals
  • Squash: 0 gold, 2 silver, 3 bronze — 5 medals
  • Sailing: 0 gold, 1 silver, 2 bronze — 3 medals
  • Cricket: 2 gold — 2 medals
  • Hockey: 2 gold — 2 medals
  • Kabaddi: 2 gold — 2 medals
  • Golf: 1 gold, 1 silver — 2 medals
  • Weightlifting and wushu: 1 silver each
  • Badminton, kurash, mixed martial arts, rowing, sepaktakraw, soft tennis and table tennis: 1 bronze each

The gold winners

India's golds span the full arc of the Games. The women's cricket team, led by Harmanpreet Kaur, opened the country's gold account by beating Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final. The men's side followed with its own title, while both kabaddi teams and both hockey teams completed clean sweeps of their events.

In shooting, Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh took the mixed 10m air pistol, Neeru Dhanda won the women's trap, and Chenai and Dhanda paired up for the mixed trap title. Boxing golds went to Lovlina Borgohain (women's 75kg), Parveen Hooda (women's 65kg) and Ankush Panghal (men's 80kg). Wrestlers Sujeet Kalkal (65kg freestyle) and Aman Sehrawat (57kg) added golds, and Pranavi Urs claimed the women's individual golf title.

Context: a Games that kept growing

The Aichi-Nagoya Games, held from September 19 to October 4 across Aichi Prefecture and Nagoya City with 46 nations competing, started slowly for India — the first medals were silvers from the 10m air rifle shooting teams — before the medal count accelerated through the middle week. Several silver medals came agonisingly close to gold: Sarvesh Kushare cleared 2.25m in the men's high jump, Yashvir Singh threw a personal best of 85.72m in the javelin, and Parul Chaudhary set a national record of 9:08.67 in the 3000m steeplechase.

Diaspora angle

For Indians abroad, the Asian Games rarely command the prime-time attention of a cricket World Cup — but the 2026 campaign is the deepest proof yet that India's Olympic pipeline extends well beyond cricket. Teenagers like archers Mohod and weightlifter Mirabai Chanu's successors are names worth learning before the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.

What's next

The Games conclude with the closing ceremony on October 4. The final medal tally will shape India's seeding and qualification pathways toward the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics — Kumkum Mohod has already sealed her Olympic quota in the recurve — and will set the benchmark against which every future Indian Asian Games campaign is measured.
